ICT Governance Policy
NDIA-POL-ICT-GOV-001
Strategy, Architecture, and Governance
WoAG Protective Security Roles
Compliance with WoAG Protective Security Directions
The Accountable Authority complies with all Protective Security Directions.
The NDIA shall ensure that the Accountable Authority complies with all Protective Security Directions issued under the Protective Security Policy Framework.
PSPF
Critical
PSPF - 2
Governance
Ensure the NDIA Accountable Authority complies with all whole-of-government Protective Security Directions to maintain WoAG security standards.
Non-compliance with PSPF Directions; regulatory breach; reputational and legal risk to the NDIA
Critical
All NDIA personnel; Accountable Authority (CEO)
None
Review all PSPF Directions upon publication and incorporate into the NDIA security governance framework. Report compliance status in the annual protective security report.
None (administrative/governance control)

1. Monitor PSPF Directions published by Department of Home Affairs. 2. Brief Accountable Authority on new Directions. 3. Update NDIA security policies to reflect Directions. 4. Report compliance in annual report.
Accountable Authority (CEO)
Chief Security Officer (CSO); Chief Information Security Officer (CISO)
General Counsel; Group Manager, Technology; NDIA Security Team
All NDIA Branch Managers; Department of Home Affairs
No
Not applicable — mandatory PSPF requirement. Refer to PSPF Req 52–53 for contingency provisions only.
Accountable Authority (subject to PSPF contingency provisions)
Annual protective security report review; independent IRAP assessment; internal audit
Signed Accountable Authority acknowledgement of PSPF Directions; annual protective security report
Annual
NDIA Cyber Security Policy; NDIA Risk Management Policy; NDIA Information Security Policy
PSPF Annual Reporting Guidance (Dept of Home Affairs); NDIA Security Governance Framework
Active
Annual
PSPF update or new Direction issued; machinery-of-government change; Accountable Authority change
Chief Security Officer (CSO)
Directions are issued by the Secretary, Department of Home Affairs under the PGPA Act. All non-corporate Commonwealth entities are subject to this requirement.

Strategy, Architecture, and Governance
Entity Protective Security Roles and Responsibilities
Accountable Authority Ministerial Accountability for Protective Security
The Accountable Authority is answerable to their minister for the entity's protective security.
The NDIA shall ensure that the Accountable Authority is answerable to the responsible Minister for the entity's protective security posture and performance.
PSPF
Critical
PSPF - 6
Governance
Establish clear lines of ministerial accountability for the NDIA's protective security, ensuring executive responsibility is transparent and enforced.
Unclear accountability for security failures; breakdown in governance and ministerial oversight
High
Accountable Authority (CEO); NDIA Executive Leadership Team
None
Establish formal reporting lines from Accountable Authority to Minister covering protective security matters. Include security performance in ministerial briefings and reporting cycles.
None (administrative/governance control)

1. Document accountability arrangements in security governance framework. 2. Brief Minister on significant security events as required. 3. Include protective security in annual ministerial reporting. 4. Maintain records of ministerial briefings.
Accountable Authority (CEO)
Chief Security Officer (CSO)
General Counsel; Ministerial Liaison Office
NDIA Board; NDIA Executive; Department of Home Affairs
No
Not applicable — mandatory PSPF requirement.
Accountable Authority
Annual protective security report; ministerial briefing records; governance framework review
Annual protective security report submitted to Minister; record of ministerial briefings on security matters
Annual
NDIA Cyber Security Policy; NDIA Corporate Governance Framework
PSPF Annual Reporting Guidance; NDIA Ministerial Communications Protocol
Active
Annual
Ministerial change; significant security incident; PSPF update; machinery-of-government change
Chief Security Officer (CSO)
Ministerial accountability is a core PSPF governance obligation for all non-corporate Commonwealth entities.
NDIA-ICT-GOV-003
ICT Governance Policy
NDIA-POL-ICT-GOV-001
Strategy, Architecture, and Governance
Entity Protective Security Roles and Responsibilities
Accountable Authority Responsibility for Security Risk Management
The Accountable Authority is responsible for managing the security risks of their entity.
The NDIA shall ensure that the Accountable Authority is responsible for managing the security risks of the entity.
PSPF
Critical
PSPF - 7
Governance
Ensure ultimate responsibility for NDIA security risk management rests with the Accountable Authority, creating accountability at the highest level.
Unmanaged security risks; failure to identify and treat entity-level threats; inadequate risk governance
Critical
Accountable Authority (CEO); all NDIA operations and systems
None

The Accountable Authority must formally own the NDIA's security risk register, approve the risk tolerance, and receive regular risk reporting. Risk management must be embedded in corporate governance processes.
None (administrative/governance control)

1. Maintain enterprise security risk register. 2. Report risk status to Accountable Authority at least quarterly. 3. Obtain formal AA approval for risk tolerance and treatment decisions. 4. Include risk status in annual report.
Accountable Authority (CEO)
Chief Security Officer (CSO); Chief Information Security Officer (CISO); Chief Risk Officer
General Counsel; Audit Committee; NDIA Board
NDIA Executive Leadership Team; Department of Home Affairs
No
Not applicable — mandatory PSPF requirement.
Accountable Authority
Security risk register review; Audit Committee minutes; annual protective security report
Enterprise security risk register signed by AA; Audit Committee risk reporting records; annual report
Annual (risk register reviewed quarterly)
NDIA Risk Management Policy; NDIA Cyber Security Policy; NDIA Information Security Policy
NDIA Enterprise Risk Management Framework; ASD Risk Management Guidelines
Active
Annual
Significant new threat or vulnerability; material change to NDIA operating environment; PSPF update; security incident
Chief Security Officer (CSO)
This requirement underpins the entire NDIA security governance structure. Risk management must be integrated into the NDIA's corporate risk framework.

Strategy, Architecture, and Governance
Entity Protective Security Roles and Responsibilities
Appointment of Chief Security Officer
A Chief Security Officer is appointed and empowered to oversee the entity's protective security arrangements.
The NDIA shall appoint and empower a Chief Security Officer to oversee the entity's protective security arrangements.
PSPF
Critical
PSPF - 8
ISO/IEC 27001:2022 Cl. 5.3; NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 PM-2
Governance
Ensure a suitably qualified and empowered security executive is responsible for all protective security arrangements across the NDIA.
Absence of dedicated security leadership; uncoordinated protective security arrangements; gaps in security governance
Critical
All NDIA operations; Accountable Authority
None

Formally appoint a CSO with a documented mandate, appropriate delegation, and direct access to the Accountable Authority. CSO must have authority to direct security activities across all NDIA business lines.
None (administrative/governance control)

1. Establish CSO position and position description. 2. Issue formal instrument of appointment. 3. Document delegations and authorities. 4. Ensure CSO has direct reporting line to Accountable Authority.
Accountable Authority (CEO)
Chief Security Officer (CSO)
General Counsel; People and Culture; NDIA Security Team
All NDIA Branch Managers; Department of Home Affairs
No
Not applicable — mandatory PSPF requirement.
Accountable Authority
Position description review; instrument of appointment; organisational chart verification
Signed instrument of CSO appointment; current CSO position description; security governance framework document
Annual; on appointment or role change
NDIA Cyber Security Policy; NDIA People Security Policy; NDIA Corporate Governance Framework
PSPF Security Governance Guidance; NDIA Delegations Framework
Active
Annual
CSO departure or appointment; restructure; PSPF update; significant change to security environment
Chief Security Officer (CSO)
The CSO must be empowered with sufficient authority and resources to fulfil their mandate. The PSPF requires the CSO to be a separate role from the CISO.

Entity Protective Security Roles and Responsibilities
CSO Seniority and Minimum Security Clearance
The Chief Security Officer is a Senior Executive Service officer and holds a minimum security clearance of Negative Vetting 1.
The NDIA shall ensure that the Chief Security Officer is a Senior Executive Service officer and holds a minimum security clearance of Negative Vetting 1.
PSPF
High
PSPF - 9
ISO/IEC 27001:2022 Cl. 5.3, A.7.1; NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 PS-3
Governance
Ensure the CSO has the requisite seniority, authority and trustworthiness to perform the role and access sensitive protective security information.
CSO lacking authority or clearance to access classified information; compromised security governance at executive level
High
Chief Security Officer (CSO)
None
Verify CSO position is classified at SES Band 1 or above. Initiate and maintain a minimum NV1 security clearance through AGSVA. Monitor clearance status and initiate renewal prior to expiry.
AGSVA clearance management system integration

AGSVA; General Counsel
NDIA Executive; Department of Home Affairs
No

Accountable Authority
Personnel security register review; AGSVA clearance verification; position description review
AGSVA clearance certificate for CSO; SES classification evidence; personnel security register entry
Annual; on role appointment
NDIA People Security Policy; NDIA Personnel Security Framework
PSPF Personnel Security Guidance; AGSVA Clearance Management Guidelines
Active
Annual
CSO appointment or change; clearance approaching expiry; adverse clearance finding; PSPF update
Chief Security Officer (CSO); People and Culture
AGSVA manages all Australian Government security clearances. NV1 is the minimum required; some roles may require NV2. Clearance status must be monitored continuously.

Strategy, Architecture, and Governance
Entity Protective Security Roles and Responsibilities
CSO Accountability to Accountable Authority
The Chief Security Officer is accountable to the Accountable Authority for protective security matters.
The NDIA shall ensure that the Chief Security Officer is accountable to the Accountable Authority for all protective security matters.
PSPF
High
PSPF - 10
ISO/IEC 27001:2022 Cl. 5.3; NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 PM-2
Governance
Establish a clear and direct accountability relationship between the CSO and Accountable Authority to ensure security matters receive appropriate executive attention.
Protective security outcomes not escalated appropriately; lack of executive-level accountability for security failures
High
Chief Security Officer (CSO); Accountable Authority (CEO)
None
Formalise the CSO's accountability through documented reporting lines and governance structures. CSO must have regular direct access to the Accountable Authority to report on security matters.
None (administrative/governance control)

1. Document CSO reporting line to Accountable Authority in governance framework. 2. Schedule regular security briefings (at minimum quarterly). 3. CSO to present at Audit Committee meetings. 4. Record meetings and outcomes.
Accountable Authority (CEO)
Chief Security Officer (CSO)
General Counsel; Audit Committee Chair
NDIA Board; NDIA Executive Leadership Team
No
Not applicable — mandatory PSPF requirement.
Accountable Authority
Governance framework review; Audit Committee minutes; CSO reporting schedule
Security governance framework documenting CSO accountability; Audit Committee minutes; executive briefing records
Annual
NDIA Cyber Security Policy; NDIA Corporate Governance Framework
NDIA Security Governance Framework; NDIA Audit Committee Charter
Active
Annual
Organisational restructure; CSO change; PSPF update; Accountable Authority change
Chief Security Officer (CSO)
The CSO must have sufficient authority and direct access to the AA to escalate critical security matters without delay.

Strategy, Architecture, and Governance
Entity Protective Security Roles and Responsibilities
Appointment of Chief Information Security Officer
A Chief Information Security Officer is appointed to oversee the entity's cyber security program and the cyber security for the entity's most critical technology resources.
The NDIA shall appoint a Chief Information Security Officer to oversee the entity's cyber security program and the cyber security of its most critical technology resources.
PSPF
Critical
PSPF - 11
ISO/IEC 27001:2022 Cl. 5.3; NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 PM-2, SA-3
Governance
Ensure a dedicated executive is responsible for the NDIA's cyber security program, providing leadership and oversight of cyber security across all critical technology assets.
Absence of cyber security leadership; unmanaged cyber risk; inadequate oversight of critical ICT systems
Critical
All NDIA technology systems and data; Accountable Authority
None

Formally appoint a CISO with a documented mandate covering the cyber security program and critical technology resources. The CISO role should be separate from the CSO. Ensure the CISO has authority to direct cyber security activities across all technology systems.
None (administrative/governance control)

1. Establish CISO position and position description. 2. Issue formal instrument of appointment. 3. Define CISO mandate covering cyber security program scope. 4. Document reporting lines and delegations.
Accountable Authority (CEO)
Chief Information Security Officer (CISO)
Chief Security Officer (CSO); General Counsel; Group Manager, Technology
All NDIA Branch Managers; Australian Signals Directorate
No
Not applicable — mandatory PSPF requirement (Modified effective 01/07/2025).
Accountable Authority
Position description review; instrument of appointment; cyber security program documentation review
Signed CISO appointment instrument; CISO position description; cyber security program charter
Annual; on appointment or role change
NDIA Cyber Security Policy; NDIA ICT Strategic Plan; NDIA Information Security Policy
ASD CISO Responsibilities Guide; NDIA Cyber Security Program Charter; NDIA Delegations Framework
Active
Annual
CISO departure or appointment; significant change to cyber threat environment; PSPF update; new critical systems
Chief Information Security Officer (CISO)
PSPF Req 11 was Modified effective 01/07/2025. The CISO mandate must explicitly cover the most critical technology resources as identified in the NDIA Technology Asset Register.

Strategy, Architecture, and Governance

CISO Capability, Experience and Minimum Security Clearance
The Chief Information Security Officer has the appropriate capability and experience and holds a minimum security clearance of Negative Vetting 1.

High
Chief Information Security Officer (CISO)
None

AGSVA; Chief Security Officer (CSO)
NDIA Executive; Australian Signals Directorate
No

Personnel security register review; AGSVA clearance verification; capability assessment documentation
CISO capability evidence (CV, qualifications); AGSVA clearance certificate; personnel security register entry
Annual; on appointment
NDIA People Security Policy; NDIA Personnel Security Framework; NDIA Cyber Security Policy
PSPF Personnel Security Guidance; AGSVA Clearance Management Guidelines; ASD CISO Responsibilities Guide
Active
Annual
CISO appointment or change; clearance approaching expiry; significant change in required capabilities; PSPF update
Chief Information Security Officer (CISO); People and Culture
Capability requirements should reference ASD's CISO Responsibilities guide and relevant SFIA competency frameworks. Clearance must be maintained continuously.

Strategy, Architecture, and Governance
Entity Protective Security Roles and Responsibilities
CISO Accountability for Cyber Security Risks
The Chief Information Security Officer is accountable to the Accountable Authority for cyber security risks and how the entity's cyber security program is managing these risks.
The NDIA shall ensure that the Chief Information Security Officer is accountable to the Accountable Authority for cyber security risks and how the cyber security program is managing those risks.

Critical
PSPF - 13
Governance
Ensure cyber security risk accountability is maintained at the Accountable Authority level, with the CISO providing regular and transparent reporting on risk posture and program effectiveness.
Cyber security risks not escalated to the Accountable Authority; inadequate executive oversight of cyber risk; governance failures
High
Chief Information Security Officer (CISO); Accountable Authority (CEO)
None

Formalise CISO accountability to the Accountable Authority through documented reporting structures. CISO must provide regular cyber security risk briefings to the AA and Audit Committee, with reporting on cyber security program performance.
Cyber security risk management platform; security metrics and dashboards

1. Document CISO reporting line to Accountable Authority. 2. Schedule regular cyber security risk briefings. 3. CISO reports on risk posture at each Audit Committee meeting. 4. Maintain records of all risk briefings and decisions.

Chief Information Security Officer (CISO)
Chief Security Officer (CSO); Audit Committee; Chief Risk Officer
NDIA Board; NDIA Executive; Australian Signals Directorate
No
Not applicable — mandatory PSPF requirement (Modified effective 01/07/2025).
Accountable Authority
Audit Committee minutes; CISO risk reporting records; cyber security program status reports
Cyber security risk register; CISO briefing records to AA; Audit Committee minutes; cyber security program status reports
Annual; cyber risk reporting reviewed at each Audit Committee meeting
NDIA Cyber Security Policy; NDIA Risk Management Policy; NDIA Information Security Policy
ASD CISO Responsibilities Guide; NDIA Audit Committee Charter; NDIA Cyber Security Program Charter
Active
Annual
Significant cyber incident; material change to NDIA's risk profile; CISO change; PSPF update; new critical systems
Chief Information Security Officer (CISO)

Security Practitioner Capability, Empowerment and Resourcing
Where appointed, security practitioners are appropriately skilled, empowered and resourced to perform their designated functions.
The NDIA shall ensure that, where appointed, security practitioners are appropriately skilled, empowered and resourced to perform their designated security functions.

High
PSPF - 14
Governance
Ensure security practitioners across the NDIA have the skills, authority and resources necessary to perform their security functions effectively.
Security practitioners unable to perform duties effectively; skill gaps leading to inadequate security controls; under-resourced security functions
High
All designated security practitioners across the NDIA
Personnel not in designated security practitioner roles

Establish competency frameworks for all security practitioner roles. Assess capability on appointment and annually. Provide adequate budget, staffing and tooling. Document delegations and authorities for each practitioner role.
None (administrative/governance control); security tooling and platforms as required by role

Group Manager, Technology; Business Area Managers

Not applicable — mandatory PSPF requirement.

Security practitioner competency assessments; resourcing plans; delegation instruments; training records

NDIA People Security Policy; NDIA Workforce Plan; NDIA Cyber Security Policy
PSPF Workforce Management Guidance; NDIA Capability Development Framework

Annual

Security Practitioner Access to Government Training
Where appointed, security practitioners have access to training across government to maintain and upskill on new and emerging security issues.
The NDIA shall ensure that, where appointed, security practitioners have access to government security training to maintain and upskill on new and emerging security issues.

All designated security practitioners across the NDIA

All NDIA security governance structures and committees; Accountable Authority
None

PSPF Security Governance Guidance; NDIA Security Governance Framework
Active

ISM and supporting cyber security control baseline

NDIA systems must select, implement, maintain and evidence the applicable ISM and supporting cyber security control baseline before operational use; any control gap must have an approved treatment, compensating control or residual risk acceptance.

Each NDIA system must know which ISM controls apply and must implement those controls before the system is used. Any control that cannot be met must have an approved risk treatment, compensating control or risk acceptance.

NDIA information and ICT assets must be identified, classified, marked, collected, used, disclosed, shared, stored, retained, transferred, sanitised, destroyed and disposed of lawfully and securely according to sensitivity, privacy, records, NDIS, FOI and protective security obligations.

NDIA must know what information and ICT assets it holds, classify them correctly and protect them throughout their life cycle from collection and storage through sharing, archiving, disposal and media handling.
Mandatory policy requirement
Critical

NDIA must continuously identify, prioritise, remediate and verify vulnerabilities, misconfigurations and unsupported technology through risk-based scanning, patching, hardening, exception management and accountable remediation tracking.
